overview:
Donald Norcross, the Democratic incumbent, is running for re-election in a South Jersey district that leans Democratic by about ten points. His Republican challenger, Damon Galdo, has run a minimal campaign, raising roughly $11,000 compared with Norcross's $1.66 million and a cash-on-hand edge of more than $2.3 million. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent, and prediction markets put his chances at about 94 percent.

With no public polls or expert ratings for this race, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. All of these point the same direction, making this a Safe Democratic seat, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
